t.7.77.1: Having thus narrated in full the entire account of the slaying of Vṛtra, Lakṣmaṇa, best of men, began the remainder of the tale.
t.7.77.3: Having taken refuge at the edge of the worlds, he, bereft of his senses and unconscious, dwelt there for some time, writhing like a serpent.
t.7.77.2: Then, when Vṛtra of great valor, the terror of the gods, had been slain, Śakra, the slayer of Vṛtra, enveloped by the sin of slaying a brahmin, could not regain his senses.
t.7.77.4: Then, when Sahasrākṣa had vanished, the world became agitated, and the earth looked as if ravaged, without moisture, its forests dried up.
t.7.77.5: The water-bearing streams, the lakes and likewise the rivers became bereft of their currents, and a great agitation arose among living beings, caused by the lack of rain.
t.7.77.6: But as this world was wasting away, the gods, their minds bewildered, undertook that sacrifice which Viṣṇu had spoken of before.
t.7.77.7: Then all the hosts of the gods, together with their preceptors and accompanied by the sages, went in a body to that place where Indra lay bewildered by fear.
t.7.77.8: But they, seeing the thousand-eyed one stupefied by the sin of brahmin-slaying, placed that lord of the gods at their head and performed a horse sacrifice.
t.7.77.9: Then, O lord of men, a very great Aśvamedha of the great-souled Mahendra was performed, for the purpose of purifying him from the sin of brahmin-slaying.
t.7.77.11: Then the gods, pleased and filled with delight, said to her: "O unassailable one, divide yourself into four parts by your own power."
t.7.77.10: Then, at the completion of the sacrifice, Brahmahatyā, the sin of brahmin-slaying that clung to the great-souled one, approached and spoke these words: “Where will you appoint a place for me?”
t.7.77.12: Having heard the words of the great-souled gods, Brahmahatyā, so hard to dwell with, chose in their presence a dwelling place elsewhere.
t.7.77.13: With one portion I shall dwell in rivers brimming with water, and with the second in trees; this truth I declare to you.
t.7.77.14: As for this third portion of mine, I, the destroyer of pride, shall dwell for three nights in women who are graced with youth and filled with pride.
t.7.77.15: But those who will deliberately kill brāhmaṇas who have done no wrong, them I shall enter and dwell in with my fourth portion, O bulls among the gods.
t.7.77.16: Then the gods replied to her: "O you who are hard to abide, let all of it be just as you say; accomplish whatever you desire."
t.7.77.17: Then the gods, filled with joy, paid homage to the thousand-eyed one, and Vāsava became free of fever, his sin purified.
t.7.77.18: When the thousand-eyed one was reestablished, the whole world became tranquil, and then Śakra honored that sacrifice of wondrous appearance.
t.7.77.19: Such indeed is the power of the Aśvamedha, O Raghunandana; therefore, O most fortunate one, O king, perform the horse sacrifice.
